Body updated. Worker has the green light on option A and is continuing on the orphan walk, TTL, archived marker, idempotency, oneoff checkpoints, and sweep. I'll be auto-invoked when they ping back.

1) I want all local sessions on a given computer to auto resume
2) what is the conterpart session name?

Quick on (2), then I need to check one thing before answering (1) cleanly.

**(2) Counterpart session**: it's `oneoff-mini-1c561b44` — picker title `[AH] oneoff-mini-1c561b44`, `cse_0194L9v2amdPMtmc8Wn1rChC`, worker=running, anchored at `~/dev/ai-harness`. That's the only one I spawned.

On (1) — "all local sessions auto-resume" — I want to check exactly what `session_resume.py` and `claude -r` can actually do today before I tell the worker to course-correct, since the original auto-resume mechanism I spec'd (preloading a transcript at `mm-*` server spawn) was the part the CLI doesn't support.

There's a hard constraint to surface before we re-spec, with a concrete proposal:

**The constraint.** Per the docstring in `session_resume.py:5-10`, there's no public API to "promote a local uuid into a fresh `cse_`" — the cloud Claude Code service has no endpoint to seed a new session from a stored transcript. So **auto-resuming back into the desktop/mobile picker row is not achievable** with today's APIs. The picker rows for prior sessions stay dead after reboot.

**What IS achievable** for "auto-resume on this computer": `session_resume.py:70-74` already has `terminal_open_argv()` — it spawns `open -na Terminal.app --args zsh -lc "cd <cwd> && claude -r <uuid>"` per forked uuid. So the realistic mechanism is: after the supervisor-startup sweep forks every orphan, it also calls `--open-terminal` on each, giving you **one Terminal.app window per recovered session, each with `claude -r <uuid>` running and the transcript pre-loaded**. Local CLI, not the cloud picker. This covers both supervisor-managed dirs and one-offs uniformly.

**The tradeoff.** On a reboot of a host with 8 prior sessions, that's 8 Terminal windows that pop up at login. TTL (24h default) filters stale ones, and the `archived` marker skips intentionally-closed sessions — but it's still noisy. Mitigation knobs: `RESUME_ON_RESTART=open-terminal|open-app|print|off` (default `open-terminal`), where `open-app` is "just bring Claude.app forward at the cwds and let the user pick", and `print` is "log the resume commands but don't spawn anything."
